title: Soak-Up Race
subject: science
learningGoal: Run a fair test to compare how well materials soak up water.
realWorldHook: Why do we use towels and not plastic to dry our hands? Some materials soak up water better.

materials.item: Strips of paper towel, printer paper and cloth
materials.householdSubstitution: Any three different papers or fabrics

noPurchaseRoute: Use any three materials you have and plain water.
parentPreview: Your child dips the ends of three strips into water at the same time and watches which one the water climbs fastest. Keeping the test fair is the main idea.

parent.parentSays: Why do we dry hands with a towel and not a plastic bag?

child.screen: Why do towels dry our hands?
child.readAloudText: Why do we dry our hands with a towel?

parent.parentSays: Which strip do you think will soak up water the fastest?

child.screen: Which strip will soak up water fastest?
child.readAloudText: Which strip will soak up water the fastest?

parent.parentSays: Cut the strips the same width and length. Dip them in at exactly the same time.
parent.whyThisWorks: Same size and same start time means only the material changes.

child.screen: Make the strips the same size. Dip them all at once!
child.readAloudText: Make the strips the same size and dip them all at once.

parent.parentSays: Watch for one minute. Which one has water climbing highest?

child.readAloudText: Look closely for one minute. Which one is winning?

parent.parentSays: Why do you think that one won?

child.readAloudText: Why did that one win? Tell your grown-up.

parent.parentSays: Ask the two check questions below. Give your child time to think, then note how each one went.
What else could we test this way?

expectedResponses: Same size strips, same start time

misconceptions.signal: Dips strips at different times or uses different sizes.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: If one strip started earlier, could we say it was the best?

misconceptions.signal: Thinks the thickest material must win.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: Was the thickest one the fastest? What else might matter?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: Why must all strips be the same size?

interpretation.clear: Explains it keeps the test fair.

child.screen: Why make all the strips the same size?
child.readAloudText: Why make all the strips the same size?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: Which would be best for mopping a spill: a sponge or a plastic plate?

interpretation.clear: Chooses sponge and links to the test.

child.readAloudText: What's best for mopping a spill? A sponge or a plastic plate?

extension: Try tissues, kitchen roll brands or an old sock. Make a chart of results.
accessibilityAdaptations: Use food colouring so the water line is easier to see.

hazards: Spilled water can make floors slippery
safety.supervision: An adult stays at the table. Scissors are used only by the adult.
stopConditions: Water spills on the floor (dry it first)
Anyone tries to drink the coloured water
safety.cleanup: Pour water away, put wet strips in the bin, wipe the table.
